newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL noon rubber mixed, anticipates INRO support.
newsitem.headline: KL noon rubber mixed, anticipates INRO support.

text.p: Malaysia's rubber market was mixed at midday, with local dealers bidding for small purchases of the SMR20 in anticipation of imminent support for the grade from INRO, traders said.

They said shortcovering demand was quite visible for the SMR20 as the International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO) was poised to buy up the grade anytime if the five-day average price of rubber dipped to 172 cents or below.
"It's mostly local dealers' shortcovering though, not fresh demand from overseas," said a trader.
At midday, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board (MRELB) quoted the benchmark RSS1 buyer for August at 228.50 cents (90 U.S. cents) a kg, up half cent from Friday's close.
The board, however, quoted the SMR 20 buyer for August half cent lower at 232 cents.
Traders quoted the SMR 20 at 234 cents, SMR CV at 295, SMR L at 278, SMR5 at 245, SMR10 at 237 and drum latex at 193.
The INRO's five-day average price was at 182.07 cents a kg on July 11, compared to the 182.48 cents on July 10.
Malaysian-based shipping brokers quoted freight rates for rubber from Malaysia to Rotterdam at $700 per 20-ft container, and $1,400 per 40-ft container.
